translation: (In the Nanjing they are written as yin-luo and yang-luo.) Altogether twenty-seven qi, following one another up and down, like the flow of a spring, like the movement of the sun and moon, without rest. Therefore the yin vessels nourish the five zang-organs, and the yang vessels nourish the six fu-organs; yin and yang connect with each other in succession, like a ring without beginning or end, no one knows [their] limits, ending and then beginning anew [like summer]. Its flowing and overflowing qi enters the extraordinary meridians, being mutually irrigated and circulated around; internally it warms the zang and fu, and externally it moistens the couli (interstices).
